# watchpoint_composite_alert_rule (Resource)

**Deprecated.** A composite alert rule that fires when a combination of monitor conditions trips together under AND / OR / N-of-M logic. Composite rules are no longer evaluated by the platform, so an existing rule never fires, and this resource will be removed in a future release. Express the same combination as an SGL alert rule and use `watchpoint_sgl_alert_rule` instead (Alerting, `/alerting/rules`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# DEPRECATED. Composite rules are no longer evaluated by the platform, so the
# rule below is stored and never fires. It still applies cleanly against the
# retained API so existing configurations keep working; migrate to the
# watchpoint_sgl_alert_rule underneath it.
resource "watchpoint_composite_alert_rule" "example" {
  name             = "Core services degraded"
  logic            = "Or"
  alert_profile_id = "ap_001"

  conditions = [
    { monitor_id = "mon_api", monitor_type = "HttpApi", fail_status = "Critical" },
    { monitor_id = "mon_db", monitor_type = "Tcp", fail_status = "Critical" },
  ]
}

# The same rule as an SGL alert rule. Every check result is written into the
# `logs` pillar carrying monitor.id and check.status, which is what makes the
# composite conditions expressible as one query: dcount over the monitor id is
# the count of distinct monitors that reported a failing check in the window.
# The summarize is deliberately ungrouped, so the rule opens ONE alert for the
# whole group the way a composite rule did, instead of one alert per monitor.
resource "watchpoint_sgl_alert_rule" "example_migrated" {
  name        = "Core services degraded"
  description = "1 of the 2 selected monitors reported a failing check within the last 5 minutes."

  sgl_query = <<-SGL
    logs
    | where attributes.check_status in ('critical', 'error', 'timeout') and attributes.monitor_id in ('mon_api', 'mon_db')
    | summarize failing=dcount(attributes.monitor_id)
  SGL

  # logic maps onto the threshold, not onto the query:
  #   logic = "Or"   -> threshold 1 (any one condition failing)
  #   logic = "And"  -> threshold = the number of monitors listed
  #   logic = "NOfM" -> threshold = min_fail_count
  operator  = "gte"
  threshold = 1

  # fail_status maps onto the check_status list. The list above is the failing
  # set; add 'warning' to it for conditions that used fail_status = "Warning".
  # monitor_type has no equivalent and needs none, because every check type
  # writes the same monitor.id and check.status attributes.
  severity = "Critical"

  # time_window_seconds -> time_range. 5m is the evaluator's shortest window, so
  # this counts monitors that failed anywhere inside the window rather than
  # monitors that are down at the same instant. cooldown_minutes has no
  # equivalent; interval_seconds is the evaluation cadence.
  time_range       = "5m"
  interval_seconds = 300

  alert_profile_id = "ap_001"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `conditions` (Attributes List) Monitor conditions combined by this rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `name` (String) Human-readable rule name.

### Optional

- `alert_profile_id` (String) Alert profile used to dispatch notifications. Omit for status-only tracking.
- `cooldown_minutes` (Number) Cooldown (minutes) between re-triggers. Defaults to `5`.
- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `logic` (String) Combination logic. One of `And`, `Or`, `NOfM`. Defaults to `And`.
- `min_fail_count` (Number) Minimum failing conditions required to trip the rule (used with `NOfM`). Defaults to `1`.
- `time_window_seconds` (Number) Window (seconds) within which conditions must be failing together. Defaults to `0`.

### Read-Only

- `alert_profile_name` (String) Resolved name of the attached alert profile.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Composite alert rule ID.
- `last_evaluated_at` (String) Timestamp the rule was last evaluated (RFC 3339).
- `last_triggered_at` (String) Timestamp the rule last triggered (RFC 3339).
- `status` (String) Current rule status (`OK`, `Triggered`, `Acknowledged`).
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Required:

- `monitor_id` (String) Monitor whose status feeds this condition.

Optional:

- `fail_status` (String) Check status that counts as failing for this condition. One of `Success`, `Warning`, `Critical`, `Error`, `Timeout`. Defaults to `Critical`.
- `monitor_name` (String) Optional cached monitor name for display.
- `monitor_type` (String) Monitor type. One of `HttpApi`, `Ssl`, `Synthetic`, `Dns`, `Tcp`, `Ping`. Defaults to `HttpApi`.
- `time_window_override_seconds` (Number) Optional per-condition override of the rule time window (seconds).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_composite_alert_rule.example rule_001
```
